channel.title: The Lowndes Signal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Lowndes Signal (lowndessignal.com)

item.title: Hannah Brady earns collegiate honors
item.description: Hope Hull’s Hannah Brady named to Freed-Hardeman University dean’s list for fall 2025; the senior is pursuing a degree in family and child sciences.

item.title: Amy's guide to effortless entertaining
item.description: Overwhelmed by a “small” dinner turning into 12 guests with picky diets? Amy shares sarcastic “bad advice” and real tips for simple, low-stress hosting that values welcome over perfection.

item.title: No-fee college applications open statewide
item.description: Alabama high school seniors can apply to many colleges for free Feb. 23–27 in the Spring 2026 Alabama College Application Campaign.

item.title: Residents discuss safety at 'Be Ready' workshop
item.description: Lowndes County residents refine severe-weather plans at “Be Ready” workshop, learning alert basics, building home kits and receiving free NOAA radios as a new mass notification system nears.

item.title: Alabama rolls out chipped EBT cards
item.description: Alabama DHR is issuing new chip-enabled EBT cards statewide, requiring activation and defaulting to in-state, in-store use only unless cardholders unlock other options.

item.title: Williams wins Athlete of the Week
item.description: Lowndes Academy senior Cami Williams is voted Lowndes County Athlete of the Week for round 23, earning 49% of 388 votes and recognition as a team-first player.

item.title: Hope ministry to hold first 2026 graduation
item.description: Hope Inspired Ministries will host its first 2026 Lowndes County graduation March 5 at 6 p.m. at Hayneville Christian Church, with the community invited and new students now being enrolled.

item.title: Lowndes County Arrests Feb. 18 - 22
item.description: Lowndes County authorities report arrests from Feb. 18–22, including child endangerment, swatting, disorderly conduct, DUI, and firearm and drug charges.

item.title: Commission resumes Zoom amid technical difficulties
item.description: Lowndes County Commission resumes Zoom meetings despite audio glitches, hears funding requests for local teams and charities, and backs a new Lowndesboro garbage pickup agreement.

item.title: Gov. Ivey recognizes Annual Doe Rodeo
item.description: Gov. Kay Ivey issues proclamation recognizing the Annual Doe Rodeo, a Cornwallis 1828 event that links conservation with providing protein to families in need across Alabama’s Black Belt.
